Let’s talk about something that can totally change the way you see your day-to-day life. This is Chapter 5—Living with an Eternal Perspective.
Most people, if we’re honest, move through life as if what we see right now is all there is. We chase after success, comfort, and security, and the days just blur together. Before you know it, the years slip by faster than you ever thought possible. But every once in a while, something happens that shakes us awake—a loss, a diagnosis, or maybe just a sudden moment of clarity. Suddenly, all those things that seemed so important? They lose their grip. And you start asking yourself: What really matters? I think about a retired couple I know. After decades of working hard, they finally had all the free time they’d dreamed of. They traveled, spent time with family, enjoyed the rewards of their labor. But after a while, the novelty wore off. They started to wonder—Is this it? So, they began volunteering at a local food bank, meeting people whose lives were marked by struggle and resilience. And in those moments, they felt a sense of purpose that no vacation could ever match. Life is short, and none of us really knows how much time we have. Most people don’t like thinking about their own mortality, but pretending it’s not real doesn’t make it go away. The truth is, we’re all just passing through. What we do with our time—it matters. When you start looking at life with an eternal perspective, everything shifts. It’s not about what you can get, but what you can give. Not about chasing temporary pleasures, but making a lasting impact. There’s a story of a teenager who faced the loss of a close friend. She was heartbroken and full of questions that just didn’t have answers. But in the middle of that pain, she realized life was too precious to waste on things that didn’t matter. She started reaching out to others—offering kindness, a listening ear, simple support. It wasn’t dramatic, but it was real. And she discovered that even the smallest acts of love can ripple out, touching lives in ways she never imagined. Now, living with an eternal perspective doesn’t mean ignoring today or pretending pain isn’t real. It’s about seeing each day as a gift—an opportunity to make a difference. It’s about holding things loosely, knowing nothing here lasts forever. It’s about investing in people, in relationships, in things that will outlast the fleeting pleasures of this world. There’s also a doctor I admire. For years, he chased after success and recognition. But eventually, he realized his real impact wasn’t in the awards or the paycheck—it was in the lives he touched. He started mentoring younger colleagues, taking time to listen, to encourage. And the more he focused on serving others, the more fulfilled he became. Most of us don’t even notice how quickly time is passing—until it’s almost gone. That’s the challenge: to live with intention, to make choices that reflect what really matters. It’s about letting go of the need for control, and trusting there’s a bigger story at work. Here’s the beautiful thing: an eternal perspective brings freedom. It frees you from comparing yourself to others, from feeling like you always have to keep up or impress. It shifts your focus to what really lasts—love, kindness, generosity, faith. It’s not about being perfect, or having all the answers. It’s about living each day with purpose, knowing that every moment counts. So, the invitation is simple—live with your eyes wide open. See beyond what’s right in front of you, and invest in what truly matters. Let go of what’s temporary, and grab hold of what’s eternal. For anyone willing to take that step, life becomes an adventure—full of risk, sacrifice, and real, lasting joy.
